rederive.empty_value: Not the same as unset. rinzler logs 'RZ_KV_CACHE_GB set to '. std::stoull then throws std::invalid_argument. main has no try block around the call. The terminate handler logs a backtrace and calls abort (src/common/backtrace.cpp:33-36, installed at src/rinzler.cpp:4548).

'Trying to use <N> GB for persistent KV cache (covering all models)' (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache.cpp:456) shows the number when the cache object is created. That line is also printed in arena mode, where the number is then not used. The warning 'Arena allocator (pos_heap_v2) is active; ignoring static KV cache sizing knob RZ_KV_CACHE_GB' (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache_control.cpp:76-80) shows that the value is ignored.

The cache target is set to the largest int64 value and one warning is logged (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache_control.cpp:60-88). Arena mode is the build default (option TRON_ARENA_ALLOCATOR_DEFAULT_ON is ON, src/system/CMakeLists.txt:86), and TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR selects the mode at run time (src/system/memory.cpp:93-97). The mode is set in pos_heap_setup, which only the real device library calls (src/pos/driver.cpp:290). So on a default build of rinzler the variable has no effect unless TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR holds a value other than 1. In rinzler_host, rinzler_mock and rinzler_proxy arena mode stays off. rinzler_host contains the token cache code (fake_scheduler_static, src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:431-433), so the value is used there. rinzler_mock and rinzler_proxy read and store the value, but their scheduler libraries do not contain the token cache code (src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:440-452), and I found no user of the value in them. 2. The flag --kv-cache-gb is parsed later and writes the same variable, so the flag wins (src/system/system.cpp:2046-2048). The flag can be on the command line. For the real rinzler it can also be inside SYSTEM_CONFIG. 3. runtron has the flags --kv-cache-gb and --kv-cache-bytes instead (src/runtron.cpp:625-636). 4. The host package drop-in sets the value 1 (packaging/tron-host/90-rinzler-host.conf:19).

Its source says: a comma list of LEVEL or NAME=LEVEL; level names trace, debug, info, warning or warn, error or err, critical, off; case is ignored; an empty value is the same as unset; an unknown level name is ignored silently. A message is written only if it passes the logger level and also the output level (spdlog include/spdlog/logger.h:262, logger-inl.h:135-137). So SPDLOG_LEVEL can only reduce logging. Example: SPDLOG_LEVEL=warn hides info and debug lines. SPDLOG_LEVEL=trace alone shows nothing more, because the outputs stay at debug.

doc_mentions.claim: On SIGUSR1 a process traces to tron::perfetto_trace_dest, which defaults to "traced" (the system backend). Setting TRACE_FILE=/path switches to the in-process backend: the process writes that file itself and ignores the .cfg file. Use it only for a capture without the daemons (line 212).
The TRACE_FILE variable sets tron::perfetto_trace_dest in pos_startup_host() (src/pos/driver.cpp). The default is "traced".
With TRACE_FILE set to a path, a SIGUSR1 capture lasts the 10 s window. Line 67: for an external capture leave TRACE_FILE unset or set it to "traced".

With TRACE_FILE unset or "traced", the SIGUSR1 tracer joins a traced session, and a set TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES then ends rinzler. With TRACE_FILE naming a path, the capture records in-process and TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES applies (line 301). Line 269 lists this case.
The in-process file backend used by --trace FILE, --trace-gen FILE and TRACE_FILE enables the periodic file writer with the 5,000 ms default of Perfetto v57.2.
With TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES set and TRACE_FILE unset or "traced", the SIGUSR1 of perfetto/wrapper ends rinzler.
rinzler-capture.sh refuses a rinzler started with a TRACE_FILE other than "traced".
In-process captures from TRACE_FILE read the buffer statistics during capture, so the last snapshot can predate the end of the trace.
